fixture_kind: evaluator durability slice (temporary file-backed store with a WAL)

tasks.instruction: Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3, all in one process, then verify the store from disk. Nothing is interrupted; this is the control.
Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3. The process may die inside the write of r2; if it does, restart from disk, recover, and abandon that write. Report what recovery found.
Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3. The process may die inside the delete of r3; if it does, restart, recover, and abandon that delete, so r3 must still be there afterwards.

Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3, then verify the store from disk. The process may die while recovery is rebuilding the store from the log; restart and recover again, and finish with one line per committed record.
Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3. The process dies twice: once inside the write of r2 and once inside recovery. Restart after each, and finish with a store that matches the log exactly once.

Write r1 twice -- the second call retries the first with the same transaction id after an ambiguous acknowledgement -- then write r4 and delete r3. Nothing is interrupted, and the store must end with one entry per record.

Delete r5, then a stale retry writes r5 again. The store's rule is that a committed deletion is final: after recovery r5 must be gone and no later write may bring it back. r3 comes from the planted history and must stay.

The log this process inherits already has damage in the middle: a torn frame sits after the committed history. Write r1 and r4 anyway, then recover. Entries that follow unverifiable bytes may not be treated as committed, so report the damage and keep only the verifiable prefix.
Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3. The process may die while the commit marker for r2 is being written; if it does, restart, recover, and abandon that write, so r2 is not durable.

Write r1, r2 and r4 and delete r3. The process dies just after the commit marker for r2 reached the file, so r2 is durable even though the call never returned. Restart, recover, and do not write r2 a second time.

preregistration.spec: product spec v1.1.0, C-02-AC3 (deletion and restore over the memory stores)
preregistration.derived_from: extends M5-B4-slice-2 (B4D). That slice interrupted a restore inside a record write; this one asks whether the write survives a process death at all, on a real file with a write-ahead log.

sample_counts.note: deterministic executions, not independent samples: each crash lands at one fixed byte, every scenario runs once, and no confidence interval is implied or may be computed from these counts

scoring.wal_integrity: the reported damage class and committed set must match the bytes on disk; damage may not be omitted or invented
scoring.durability: every committed record must be in the store after the final recovery
scoring.uncommitted_write: a record whose transaction never committed may not be in the store and may not be left as a record line
scoring.duplicate_effects: one line per record: a replay that applies a committed entry twice fails
scoring.resurrection: a committed deletion is final; no later write may restore the record
scoring.unrelated_record: records that were committed before the crash and are not part of the interrupted write must survive it
scoring.recovery_complete: the final store must be the committed set, with no residue, and completeness may only be claimed when it is true

thresholds.C-02-AC3: 0 residual copies, 0 resurrections, 0 lost committed records, 0 applied uncommitted writes, 0 duplicate effects, 0 unresolved recoveries

provenance.note: records are invented vendor claims in a temporary directory; the store is evaluator code, not J.A.R.V.I.S. storage; no file outside the temporary directory is read or written

crash_schedule.rule: the fixture declares the candidate stages and the interrupted operation; the evaluator picks the stage from sha256(task:salt:attempt) and a byte offset strictly inside that operation's bytes, so the same task always crashes at the same byte
crash_schedule.gold: the fixture declares the end state; the loader recomputes it for every candidate stage and refuses the fixture if any candidate disagrees
crash_schedule.solver_view: the solver sees the instruction, the records, the planted history and the operations. It does not see the candidates, the salt, the chosen stage, the byte offset or the expected outcome

state_model.rule: a record is committed when its entry frame and its commit frame are both verifiable on disk; a torn or corrupt frame leaves it not_started; a record line with no commit is partially_applied residue and is removed by recovery; a committed deletion rolls the record back and is final
recoverable: record line with no commit marker
